name: font-shirokumagen
description: Supplies the ShirokumaGen Term font — HackGen Console refitted so that no symbol a terminal draws one cell wide is ever squashed sideways: a width-1 code point upstream drew on the full-width advance 1080 now advances exactly one 540-unit cell (measured: 1656 glyphs of the regular face, 1621 of the bold), ink wider than 1.15 cells is scaled down to that width, and a refitted glyph's height is scaled by up to 1.3 times its width factor — capped, per glyph, so the stretch never carries it past the top or bottom edge of the face's own 漢, which means the refit pushes nothing past that kanji and leaves a glyph that was already past it with the shape equal scaling gives it (measured: 0 glyphs newly outside; 1128 of the 1723 refitted glyphs in the regular face grew taller, 1115 of 1694 in the bold, the rest had no room left; and 593 of the regular face's were outside the kanji's box to begin with, so this is not a claim that nothing reaches further than 漢 — and that is a statement about the vertical factor, not about the bytes: all 593 are refit targets, 573 of them had their advance set to the cell, and only 8 are unchanged to the unit against upstream), ink reaching past its cell is centred so the overhang is symmetric and at most about 7.6% of a cell per side (measured; the ratio alone puts it at 7.5% and integer rounding on this typeface's 540-unit cell accounts for the rest), and the cell grid is unchanged — A stays 540, a full-width glyph stays 1080, and body glyphs keep both outline and advance (measured: 0 outline changes among 13,101 per face; ASCII and Latin-1 left as the typeface designed them) — to extensions that borrow a bundled monospace face. It is a resource for extension developers, not a font selectable from ordinary settings such as editor.fontFamily.
